newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt calls confidence on decree amendment.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt calls confidence on decree amendment.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government called a confidence motion on its own amendment to a decree on the transport sector, Social Affairs Minister Livia Turco told the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Thursday.

Turco said the amendment covered all parts of the measure which had not yet been discussed. Under a Constitutional Court ruling, the government can no longer roll over expiring decrees and it has resorted to confidence votes on several occasions.
The vote on the decree, which covers a reorganisation of the transport sector, cannot take place for 24 hours after being called under parliamentary rules.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government called a confidence vote earlier this week to sweep aside a raft of opposition amendments to the last part of the 1997 austerity budget.
The centre-left government, which relies on support from the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for a majority in the Chamber, has won all its confidence votes comfortably.
The government's own amendment to the transport decree would bring together a number of measures and incorporate changes to the decree presented in the Chamber's transport commission.
